list.title: What are antibodies?
list.snippet: Antibodies are proteins produced by the immune system to fight off infections like COVID-19.

list.title: What do COVID-19 antibody tests do?
list.snippet: They detect the presence of antibodies against the SARS-CoV-2 virus in a blood sample.

list.title: What can the test results tell you?

list.snippet: They can indicate if you've been infected with the virus in the past.
They can suggest if you have some level of immunity, especially after vaccination, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

list.title: What can't the test results tell you?

list.snippet: They cannot tell you if you currently have an active COVID-19 infection.
They cannot tell you if you are immune or protected from future infection, or for how long.

list.title: Why are they used?
list.snippet: Antibody tests can help scientists understand how widespread infection has been, and they can help evaluate the effectiveness of vaccines.
